title: Crown Point's Old Lake County Jail: Dillinger's Escape and the Voices in the Cells

timeline: 1882, the c. 1908 jail and 1928 addition, empty since 1974, National Register 1989

beats.text: In 1934, Crown Point's jail was supposed to be escape-proof. John Dillinger got out anyway.
beats.label: CROWN POINT, INDIANA
beats.credit: History: Old Sheriff's House Foundation; Britannica

beats.text: On March 3, he pulled a gun on his guards. Legend says he carved it from wood and blackened it with shoe polish. Some say it was real.
beats.label: MARCH 3, 1934
beats.credit: Old Sheriff's House Foundation; The Mob Museum; Britannica

beats.text: He locked more than a dozen guards and inmates in the cells, took the sheriff's own car, and fled into Illinois.
beats.label: THE GETAWAY
beats.credit: Old Sheriff's House Foundation; TIME (1934); Legends of America

beats.text: Taking a stolen car across a state line was a federal crime, so federal agents joined the hunt.
beats.label: INTO ILLINOIS
beats.credit: National Archives; Britannica; Lowell Tribune (1934); The Mob Museum

beats.text: Today you can tour the old jail. Visitors say they hear voices in the cells and footsteps in the walkways, and some say they've seen figures in the corridors.
beats.label: WHAT VISITORS SAY
beats.credit: Crown Point Community Library; American Hauntings

beats.text: Whether it's Dillinger or someone else, nobody knows.
beats.label: THE OLD LAKE COUNTY JAIL

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.

factcheck.result: Lines 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 supported. Line 3 reworded ('guards and inmates', 'fled' because a hostage deputy drove). Map: straight Crown Point-Chicago line replaced by the documented leg to Peotone, Ill., with Chicago marked where the car turned up. End card: tours are seasonal.
